verdictSummary: Substantial, mostly sound correction; not yet acceptable. Closed: RPR-2 (envelope joins), RPR-3 (governed subject3 index; independently recomputed), RPR-6 (byte codec and owner native depth), RPA-2, RPA-3, RPA-5. The envelope5/inventory5 additive declarations are true by restoration, the 43 metadata cases still pass through envelope5, and the historical metadata checker still passes. Partly closed, with required corrections: RPR-1 (fit), RPR-4 (feature states), RPR-5 (provenance), RPR-7 (byte law), RPR-8 (standing). New blocking and required issues: (1) fit parity may be a truncated candidate page, and the fit query request is unspecified; fit --ephemeral refusal changes accepted flag semantics without passage scope; the post-commit failure form is ambiguous. (2) Graph slots admit silently cut pages disclosed as complete-page-set, and the reference byte projector produces exactly that instead of re-issuing the owner query. (3) The step/attempt ledger is marked no-admitted-owner although invocation:3 StepResult/Attempt owner records exist, so an approved Preserve capability disappears behind a false reason. That is a design blocker, not implementation work. (4) Several verifiedInDocument claims are not verified, and some host claims are not disclosed. (5) The frozen subject cannot run its own checker, and envelope5 admission loads an unpinned, locally modified module. (6) Passage overrides omit passages the candidate changes. No product, M4, browser, generator or performance qualification is inferred.

RPR-1.basis: The envelope5 advisoryReport, the inventory5 advisoryDispatch and fit host admission exist; P1 is refused J-ENV-FIT-CARRIER; 15 envelope cases pass; the fit views include findings and candidate-list. Residuals are in RPR2-1.

RPR-2.basis: P2/P3/P3b are refused with owned query_surface_projection codes. candidates-latest-view is now a refusal. QueryResult equality is enforced (check.py:182-189).

RPR-3.basis: subjectIndex rows are recomputed from the governed GraphEndpoint descriptor with schemaVersion 3. An independent stdlib implementation reproduces 3/3 goldens and 5/5 audit index rows, strictly sorted. The path-lookalike file finding (subjectPath src/legacy.js, same as an indexed nativeSubjectId) does not join. Advisories A1 and A2 remain.

RPR-4.basis: Typed per-command featureStates are schema consts, and prose-only featureMap rows are refused. But F01's reason is factually false (RPR2-3), and reason vocabulary does not distinguish no-owner from not-retained or no-carrier (A5).

RPR-5.basis: Per-panel const provenance exists, and hiding it is SCHEMA-refused. P4 is refused, P7/P10 are accepted with visible host assertions. But several verifiedInDocument claims are overstated (RPR2-4).

RPR-6.basis: Byte parse with canonical.py rules; 11 lexical/byte cases; chain 27 accepted and 28 refused CODEC-OWNER-DEPTH. The report canonical() uses the same json.dumps parameters as canonical.py:67-72. My path count of native gains agrees (graph request/response 6, coverage entry 5, history finding 7-2, policy rule 7-2, registry 6). Advisories A3 and A4 remain.

RPR-7.basis: Caps are restated; worst cases reproduced (49,889 / 66,236 / 6,414,670 B); 85 worst findings refused at the 4 MiB envelope boundary shared with JSON. The history prefix is deterministic and maximal. My evidence-prefix probe is deterministic and maximal, and page-size reduction selects 50. But page reduction slices items without owner re-issue, and admission accepts the result (RPR2-2).

RPR-8.basis: Standing is 'not approval'; AUDIT-G10 stays open; overrides are conditional. contract.md:7 still claims a 'complete finite design' while RPR2-1..3 remain, and the frozen subject is not self-checking (RPR2-5).

RPA-1.basis: The static human-parity section and failure notice are specified in prose (contract.md:293-297) and in the inventory5 html parityRule. Its content has no owner shape or golden, and chapter-14 rows 459/564 are not scoped (RPR2-6, A10).

RPA-5.basis: 48 pins verified. Note A11: pins bind uncommitted working-tree bytes.

requiredFindings.title: fit carrier: parity may be a truncated candidate page with an unspecified query request; --ephemeral refusal changes accepted flag semantics without scope; post-commit failure form is ambiguous
evidence: Probe Q1 (work/probes/f_probes.json): the fit-run base with candidateList.context truncated=true, totalItems=listed+500 and nextCursor set is accepted by both admit_envelope and admit_document. So the fit 'candidates' and 'evidence-levels' parity fields can be one page of an unbounded list. CandidateListRecordV1.candidates has maxItems 1000.

advisoryDispatch fixes surface, stepKind, operations and parityPaths but no request: no view/page size/cursor/order selection for the fit query step. Only includeSuppressed=false is fixed, in FitAdvisoryReportV1. Two conforming hosts can therefore emit different fit parity for the same Run.

The inventory5 fit --ephemeral flag join is byte-unchanged: '§1: explicitly non-authoritative; cannot supply baseline/repair/verify prerequisites'. Workflows §1 lists what ephemeral cannot satisfy as baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay, and §9 scopes the golden to 'with baseline/repair prerequisite'. The new golden fit-ephemeral-no-sealed-run widens that law to fit. It is a request-semantics change to an accepted advertised flag, not an additive declaration, and no passage override or command-owner decision records it.

Workflows §8 already defines the non-authoritative parity law: run-id is explicitly null. A null or explicitly unavailable candidates alternative therefore exists and was not assessed against refusal.

Probe Q2a/Q2b (work/probes/g_probes.json): contract §3.5 row 3 (candidate step failure after commit, no advisoryReport, termination runId) is refused J-ENV-FIT-CARRIER as kind=run and accepted as kind=failure. The contract names neither kind, and no case covers it.

contract.md:104 says termination is the existing step aggregate over the analysis and query steps. contract.md:112 collapses every candidate-step refusal to operational-failed DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED. These conflict whenever the query step has its own refusal class.
ownerLines: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/workflows-and-surfaces.md:1104-1106 (fit may run authoritative analysis by default)
requiredCorrection: Specify the fit query step request completely: view {runId of the sealed Run}, includeSuppressed false, page size and cursor law.

Choose explicitly one of two parity laws and add refusal cases for it. Either fit parity requires the complete candidate set (context truncated=false, totalItems equal to listed, and a >1000-candidate result is a required-delivery failure), or truncation is part of the declared parity with truncated/totalItems/nextCursor parity paths.

For --ephemeral, either obtain a recorded command-owner decision with passage overrides (workflows §1 list, the §9 golden row and the inventory5 fit flag join), or adopt the existing non-authoritative null-parity law.
Fix the post-commit candidate failure envelope kind and add accepted and refused cases.

requiredFindings.title: Graph slots admit silently cut pages disclosed as complete-page-set; the reference byte projector slices items instead of re-issuing the owner query
evidence: Contract §8.3 step 5 requires 're-issuing the identical owner query for the same Run, params and fact views' at the smaller page size. check.py:453-456 instead copies the planned slot, sets request.page.size and slices response.items[:size]. It keeps the original response context unchanged and computes continuation from that stale context.

Probe work/probes/j_reduced_slot.json: the projector reduces a 100-row worst neighbor slot to 50 rows. The context still says truncated=false, totalItems=2 and has no nextCursor, and hostProjection is {continuation: complete-page-set, pageSizeCause: byte-budget-reduced}. The document is admitted (i_projector.json S2-admit accept).
Standalone mutation on audit-full: a slot's items are cut from 3 to 1 while context totalItems=3 and truncated=false remain, and the slot keeps complete-page-set/ladder-first. Result: accept.

Admission (check.py:309-342) never joins response.items length to context totalItems/producedItems/truncated/nextCursor. So 'visible limits' (R15) and the J-GRAPH-CONTINUATION disclosure can be false while the report admits.

The checker's own worst-case fixture op (check.py:541-550) sets 64/63/100 items under a context whose totalItems is 2. The CODEC-OWNER-BYTES and J-BUDGET-BYTES worst cases are therefore built on internally inconsistent owner responses.
ownerLines: docs/v2/architecture/prototype-report-inventory.md:113-117 (R15: visible limits; source vs host vs browser layers)
requiredCorrection: Admission must join each slot response's item count to its owner context: truncated, totalItems and producedItems, with nextCursor present iff more rows exist. It must refuse a context/items mismatch with a stable code, and add refusal cases.
The reference projector must model re-issue at the smaller page: the owner response context changes, including nextCursor and continuation not-embedded where applicable.
Rebuild the worst-case slot fixtures with consistent contexts.

requiredFindings.title: step-attempt-ledger is declared no-admitted-owner although invocation:3 owns step/attempt records; an approved Preserve capability disappears behind a false reason, and some obligations are design decisions mislabelled as implementation lanes
evidence: invocation:3 defines InvocationRecord.stepResults (invocation-record.schema.json:49), StepResult with attempts[<=3] (1144-1160) and Attempt {executionId, outcome, faultCause, retried, derivation} (1039). These are exactly the Invocation/step/attempt ledger R03 names.
R03 disposition is Preserve, and chapter 14 overview-view must 'Display admitted invocation/step/attempt summaries and outcomes without ... concealing missing child evidence'.

The candidate sets step-attempt-ledger unavailable/no-admitted-owner for all 8 commands, for example the report schema default branch at line 237. The only missing piece is a carrier: the report already embeds other owner roots as panels (comparison:2, CoverageResultV3, ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1, AnalysisResult). Root authorized feature states only 'when factual owner not available'.

RP-OBL-F01 is phrased as a future 'carrier' obligation. Choosing that carrier (an envelope member or report panel over InvocationRecord, with bounds and joins to requestId/runId) is report-owner design work, not an M1/M4 implementation lane.

By contrast, F04 (policy-document:2 Rule has no description member, line 423), F05 (ReleaseCapabilityDeclarationV1 is {capabilityId, languageModes}, line 795), F07/F08 (RecipeRef is references only, repair.schema.json:284) and F09 (no metric def found in pinned schemas) are genuine owner absences, correctly disclosed.
F11: native FrameworkRecognitionV1.entryPoints exists (native-evidence.schemas.v2.json:3857-3901). The absence is retention/query, not the owner, so the reason is imprecise (A5).
RP-OBL-F03 (multi-run selection) and RP-OBL-S01 (graph slot selection policy) are command/report design decisions. The byte law itself depends on the S01 plan order.
ownerLines: subject report-projection.schema.json:237 (default step-attempt-ledger no-admitted-owner) and the corresponding rows of each command branch
requiredCorrection: Author a bounded step/attempt ledger carrier over the owned InvocationRecord/StepResult/Attempt records, with joins to requestId and runId, missing-child disclosure and a byte-law position. Alternatively, record an explicit root decision that R03 is deferred, with a reason code that states the true cause (for example no-admitted-carrier), not no-admitted-owner.
Split obligations into design blockers (F01, F03, S01) and implementation or qualification lanes (B01, B02, H01, M01, G01, E01), and keep AUDIT-G10 open on the design blockers.

advisories.text: The subjectIndex bound 12006 = 6×(2×1000+1) (contract.md:215) uses 1000 items per slot, but the page ladder caps slots at 100 rows, and path rows carry up to 65 nodes. The bound is reachable only with owner-invalid path rows: minimum endpoint 115 B plus index row 216 B gives about 333 B per extra endpoint, so about 12,007 endpoints fit in about 4.0 MiB. It is unreachable for owner-consistent paths (about 630 B per endpoint with edges). Restate the derivation and rely on RPR2-4's path consistency check.

Endpoint discovery (check.py:207-220) is a structural key-set walk over params and items, not schema-located pointers. It is not path guessing, but a governed per-operation endpoint pointer list would make host and browser recomputation identical by construction.

Depth refusal code depends on parser recursion: nesting 39 gives CODEC-DEPTH, but nesting 200000 gives CODEC-LEXICAL (stack overflow) (work/probes/f_probes.json Q7). Specify iterative depth detection during parse so host and browser codes agree.
Native-offset gains are hard-coded in check.py:857-859 rather than derived from the schema locations. A path count agrees today but would not detect drift.

Feature-state reason vocabulary has only no-admitted-owner. F11 (owner exists, not retained or queryable), F02 (configuration owner exists, redaction owner absent) and F01 (RPR2-3) need distinct reasons so the browser does not misstate the cause.
RP-OBL-S01 fixes which graph data a report contains, which is a design choice. It is labelled an M4 lane.

The coverage overlay rechecks only the 102 commands-sourced rows. The 24 reportFeatures rows (e.g. R03/R07 'planned-behavioral-test') and 13 workflows contractSections rows are not updated to reference featureStates, F-obligations, report-projection:1 or envelope5 schema rows.

Generator implications are untested. report-projection:1 and envelope5 use object/array consts (featureStates, provenance, graphPageSizeLadder, parityPaths) and allOf-$ref narrowing (GraphSlotV1, HistoryRunV1.run, FitAdvisoryReportV1). The m1 adapter projects const through prepare.py:167-168 literal(), and render-types.cjs:34 throws on unprojected const. No generator run over these documents was performed. The AUDIT-G10 M1 decision still applies until acceptance.
Label capabilities registry-sha256-recomputed as integrity-only, not source verification.
The static human-parity section has no owner shape or golden. Add per-base expected static-section content (parity fields, termination, errors, disclosures) so B01 tests against a fixed oracle.
Pins bind the architecture working tree, which has uncommitted edits (including canonical.py, whose pinned hash matches the modified bytes). Retain those exact bytes with the acceptance record.
